attempts.summary: On node1, /srv/data is now a btrfs subvolume ("current") on a loopback-backed btrfs filesystem (/var/lib/srvdata/backing.img), mounted persistently via /etc/fstab. Populated it with application data, took a read-only snapshot (snap_baseline), then modified/corrupted the live directory (overwrote a file, deleted another, added a stray file). Restored /srv/data to the exact snapshot content using the btrfs subvolume-swap technique (demoted the corrupted subvolume, promoted a fresh writable snapshot of snap_baseline as the new "current"), and verified byte-for-byte checksum equality with the pre-modification baseline. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id and data-health baseline, issued `sudo reboot`, polled until SSH/exec access returned, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified /srv/data remounted via fstab with identical file content/checksums and all btrfs subvolumes (current, snap_baseline, corrupted history) intact post-restart.
